# Warning message for shadowed attributes is truncated

## Description

The warning message for field names that shadow attributes in parent classes is truncated. The warning message ends with a semicolon and doesn't include the class name where the field is defined.

## Reproduction

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
import warnings

# Enable all warnings
warnings.simplefilter('always')

class Parent:
    foo: bool = False

class Child(BaseModel, Parent):
    foo: bool = True  # This should trigger a warning

# Expected warning message:
# Field name "foo" in "Child" shadows an attribute in parent "Parent"

# Actual warning message:
# Field name "foo" shadows an attribute in parent "Parent";
```

The warning message is missing the class name where the field is defined (in this case "Child") and ends with a semicolon instead of properly completing the message.

This makes it harder to identify which class has the shadowing field when working with complex inheritance hierarchies.
